term: not guilty by reason of insanity
definition: Not guilty by reason of insanity is a plea or affirmative defense by excuse entered by a defendant in a criminal trial, in which the defendant claims that they were so mentally disturbed or incapacitated at the time of the offense that they did not have the required intention or mens rea to commit the crime, and are therefore not guilty. Not guilty by reason of insanity can also be a verdict entered by a jury in a criminal case, stating that the defendant cannot be liable because of the defendant’s insanity. Such a verdict may require the defendant to be admitted into a mental institution. To prove legal insanity, defendants usually put forth expert testimony on their psychological evaluation. Various jurisdictions use various tests to judge such pleas (for example: M’Naghten Rule, cognitive test, irresistible impulse test, substantial capacity test, etc.). not guilty / not guilty by reason of insanity Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026
